name: Direct Democracy
summary: Direct democracy holds that citizens should make laws and major decisions themselves, by assembly, referendum or initiative, rather than through elected representatives. Its classic statement is Rousseau's claim that sovereignty cannot be represented and that a law the people has not ratified is void. Advocates favour tools such as recall, popular initiatives and sometimes lot-chosen citizen bodies, and are usually most at home at local scale.
scope: The tradition of rule by citizens' own votes as set out by Rousseau (The Social Contract, Book III ch. 15), as practised in Athenian assemblies, New England town meetings and Swiss cantonal and federal votes, and as extended by participatory democrats such as Pateman. It is a view about how decisions are made, so most statements on economics, culture and foreign policy are answered neutral with low confidence. It excludes the representative democracy covered by the democracy profile.

sources.usedFor: Sovereignty cannot be represented; laws not ratified by the people are void; executive power may be delegated.

sources.title: Participatory democracy

sources.usedFor: Pateman and Cole on participation, citizens' assemblies chosen by lot, and hybrid models such as liquid democracy.

strong-leader.rationale: Handing authority to a leader who bypasses the people's own deliberation contradicts the principle that sovereignty cannot be delegated.

decide-locally.rationale: Assemblies are most workable at local level (town meetings, Swiss Landsgemeinden), and Rousseau thought self-rule might require a very small state.

experts-over-public.rationale: The whole case for direct democracy is that ordinary citizens can and should decide public questions themselves, and Pateman argues the belief that they cannot is mistaken.

one-party-rule.rationale: A guiding party standing in for the people's own decisions is the kind of delegation of sovereignty Rousseau rejects.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Government by a hereditary individual is incompatible with citizens making the laws themselves, though Rousseau allows executives to administer them.

democracy-best.rationale: Advocates treat direct rule by citizens as the fullest form of democracy and trust the popular vote over any guardian class.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct democracy is defined as citizens voting on policy themselves rather than through elected representatives; Rousseau holds that a law the people has not ratified in person is void.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils are a form of direct participation but the sources tie direct democracy to citizens generally, not workers alone.

natural-rulers.rationale: Direct democracy rests on citizens ruling as political equals, with no class naturally entitled to rule them.

organic-representation.rationale: Rousseau holds that sovereignty cannot be represented at all, whether by parties or by corporate bodies.

single-common-good.rationale: Rousseau's general will aims at a common good rather than the sum of private interests, but scholars dispute whether it is found by assembly or by reason, and many direct democrats are pluralists.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Pateman argues for extending participation into everyday life including organisations, but this is participatory democracy rather than direct democracy proper.

proportional-representation.rationale: Concerns representative systems, which direct democracy sets aside rather than reforms.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Rousseau argues that deputies end up selling the people out and that governments tend to usurp the general will, which is the tradition's case against rule by representatives.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal political standing for all citizens underlies the case for direct rule, although Athens and Rousseau both excluded groups such as women.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rousseau grounds legitimate law in the people's own assent in assembly, and nothing binds citizens who have not agreed to it.

separated-powers.rationale: Rousseau separates sovereign lawmaking from executive government, but Madison's criticism of pure democracy shows the checks tradition is at odds with it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Athenian sortition and modern advocates of randomly selected citizen assemblies are the tradition's main alternative to election, though many direct democrats stress votes rather than lots.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by senior clerics replaces the people's own lawmaking with an unelected authority.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is one of the core mechanisms of direct democracy, letting citizens keep control over the people they elect.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rousseau praised rural simplicity, but direct democracy as a method takes no stand on this; adherents are split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Distrust of elites is a populist theme, but direct democracy as a method takes no settled stand on this claim.

death-penalty.rationale: Direct democrats are split; Swiss voters have voted on the death penalty, so it is a matter for popular vote rather than a fixed position.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A decision-method view takes no settled stand on pornography law; adherents are split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents back popular ratification of fundamental law, as in Rousseau, but an elected assembly is itself a form of representation, so they are split on it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Direct democrats favor decision-making at local scale, and the Swiss cantons keep their own laws within a federation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereignty belongs to the citizens, and executive power is only delegated to officials; a sacred head of state contradicts the doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rousseau holds that the people alone make law and that law the people has not ratified is void, while rulers are mere agents who execute it.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Popular sovereignty means a people governs itself, and for Rousseau sovereignty cannot be handed to others, so rule over another people is hard to justify.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Direct democracy is a method of decision, and adherents split on this question; some would leave it to popular vote, as in several US ballot measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: The ideology is about who decides, not monetary policy; adherents are split and the Swiss popular votes on money show it is open to voters.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A view about how decisions are made, with no stand on capitalism's crises; adherents hold varied views.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to foreign influence; adherents are split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to this class analysis; adherents hold differing views.

minority-veto.rationale: Rousseau holds that only the founding compact needs unanimity and that the majority vote then binds the rest.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rousseau treats rulers as mere commissioned officers whom the sovereign people can appoint and remove at will.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rousseau rejects representation, calling English liberty a matter of election day only; a law not ratified by the people is void.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rousseau says that when citizens prefer private gain to public service, the state is near ruin; participation is the duty of a citizen.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Rousseau holds that deputies are only commissioners who cannot conclude anything finally, and recall is a core direct-democratic tool for keeping elected people answerable.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand; the citizens could decide this by vote.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand on population policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local assemblies could decide such rules, but the doctrine itself takes no stand.

job-guarantee.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand on economic policy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rousseau holds that obligation arises from the social contract and the general will, so there is a duty to obey laws the people made.

non-intervention.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand on foreign affairs; Rousseau stressed small-state sovereignty but adherents differ.

industrial-unions.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A theory of the general will and equal citizenship rules out singling out a minority as conspirators, and such claims are not part of the tradition.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand on marriage.

local-production.rationale: A decision-method view with no stand on production, though it favours local scale for deliberation.

informal-organisation.rationale: It works through assemblies, initiatives and referenda with formal procedures, not small informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: A decision-method view; Rousseau did propose a civil religion, but the doctrine does not define the nation by religion.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A procedural view with no stated stance on regional revenue; adherents are split.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participatory democrats such as Pateman and Cole extend direct citizen decision-making to workplaces and communities, which this statement describes.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rousseau holds that sovereignty rests in the people and that laws they have not ratified are void, which rejects authority derived from God.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Rule by citizens' own votes is incompatible with hereditary office, and Rousseau holds that sovereignty rests with the people and cannot be inherited.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement extends the vote to all citizens, and Rousseau and Pateman treat equal participation as the basis of legitimate law.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rousseau's Social Contract makes the law a general, publicly enacted rule ratified by the people, as opposed to particular decrees by rulers.

racial-franchise.rationale: Citizens as a whole make the laws, and Rousseau's general will and Athenian-style assembly rest on equal citizenship rather than a restricted group.

online-participation.rationale: Internet voting and deliberation are widely proposed as ways to scale direct participation, though some adherents prefer in-person assemblies at local scale.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Direct democrats favour ordinary citizens deciding public questions themselves, and the lot-chosen bodies of Athenian democracy and modern sortition are a recognised part of that tradition, though many prefer full popular votes to a small sample.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A method of decision-making with no settled stand on policing; citizens could vote either way.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: A method of decision-making with no settled stand on charity versus state aid.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A method of decision-making with no stand on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: A method of decision-making with no stand on religious office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: A method of decision-making with no stand on marital authority.

rent-control.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method with no settled stand on rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method with no settled stand on intellectual property.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method; it would put such questions to a vote but takes no side.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method; it would put such questions to a vote but takes no side.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method with no settled stand on economic distribution.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method with no settled stand on this moral question.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method with no settled stand on national identity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Direct democracy is a decision method with no settled stand on national commemoration.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Rousseau holds deputies can only be commissioners who carry out the people's will, which matches delegates who coordinate while decisions stay with local assemblies.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are a policy matter the tradition leaves to popular vote rather than prescribing.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Swiss-style debt brakes were adopted by referendum, but adherents are split on binding legislatures and electorates alike with fixed rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic rules are not a defining issue; adherents would let citizens vote on them.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Rousseau says a people that elects representatives is free only on election day, so choosing rulers by election is not enough for democracy.

indirect-election.rationale: Rousseau holds that sovereignty cannot be represented and that deputies cannot stand in for the people, so rule through chains of delegates is rejected in favour of citizens voting themselves.

missingStatements.text: Voters should be able to remove elected officials from office before their term ends.
missingStatements.rationale: Recall is listed among the core mechanisms of direct democracy as a way for citizens to keep control over those they elect.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be able to put a proposed law to a public vote by collecting signatures.
missingStatements.rationale: The citizens' initiative is a defining tool of direct democracy, as in Switzerland.

notes: Rousseau himself favoured an elective aristocracy for government and a very small state, so scholars dispute how fully democratic he was. Modern advocates mostly accept hybrid, semi-direct systems like Switzerland's.
